more_info.overview: Sorbitan monolaurate is used as an emulsifier in food. Its technological role is to help oil and water remain mixed.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include jam jellies and marmalades and similar products. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.origin: Made from partial esters of sorbitol and its anhydrides with lauric acid. The specification does not identify a single biological source for the fatty acid.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The fatty-acid feedstock is not specified as exclusively plant derived. Vegan, vegetarian, halal and kosher suitability cannot be established without the supplier identifying the raw material and processing.
more_info.daily_intake: 10 mg sorbitan/kg body weight/day, combined sorbitan esters (EFSA, 2017).
more_info.side_effects:
Assessed food-use exposure stayed below the group limit.
Animal toxicity evidence informed its safety margin.
